heading: Final expense insurance or a prepaid funeral plan? (69 seconds)
name: Final expense insurance or a prepaid funeral plan?
description: Final expense insurance is a small whole life policy that pays the beneficiary you name. A prepaid funeral plan is a contract with a funeral home; this short video shows who gets the money with each one and what to ask before you sign.
transcript: Final expense insurance, or a prepaid funeral plan? Here is who gets the money with each one. Final expense insurance is a small whole life policy. Burial insurance is often the same product, under a different name. It pays the beneficiary you name. A prepaid funeral plan is a contract with a funeral home. You choose services ahead of time, and pay in advance. Final expense insurance pays your named beneficiary. The money can be used for any purpose. It is not tied to a location. A prepaid plan pays the funeral home, for the items listed. It is often tied to one provider. If you move, a prepaid plan may need to be transferred or canceled. Before you sign, ask: is the plan portable if I move? Can I cancel, and what do I get back? Where is the money held? Federal rules require funeral homes to give you an itemized price list. You can generally choose only the items you want. Want to talk it through? Schedule a time at honorbrook-insurance.com or call (301) 615-8289.
